h1:
Nan Old Town Cafes
10 Doi Coffee Spots You Can Walk To
intro: Nan's charm is an old town that's still easy to walk. Most coffee shops sit within a few hundred meters of Wat Phumin, and plenty of them roast their own arabica from the doi (highlands) around the province, set up inside old wooden houses or Lanna-style homes. You can sip a coffee, then keep wandering and shooting photos all morning. We picked 10 spots in town that locals and travelers actually talk about, and we'll tell you straight which one suits who.

blocks.html: Nan doesn't do the heavily-designed cafes you get in Chiang Mai, but it has something a lot of towns don't: small shops in old wooden houses right in the old town, where the owner roasts the beans and knows the doi they came from. Walk a few minutes out from Wat Phumin and you'll pass several of them. Early in the day, when the air's still nice, grab a cup and head out to shoot the old walls and gateway arches.

blocks.text: Ranking the Cafes in Nan Old Town

blocks.html: We've ordered these by how easy they are to walk to from the Wat Phumin area and how often people bring them up, easiest and most-talked-about first. Each one has its own character, so read through and pick the style you like.

items.name: Erabica Coffee
items.blurb: The cafe most Nan locals name before any other, right in the center of town. Vintage-meets-modern decor, using arabica from Nan's own doi. The drink people order most is the Chinese gooseberry (Chinese plum) coffee, an oddly good sweet-and-sour mix, alongside pour-overs and waffles. The interior shoots well too.
items.meta: In town, walkable from Wat Phumin · coffee around ฿55–90

items.name: inlamai coffee
items.blurb: On Pha Kong Road in the center of town, decorated homey-minimal, airy and quiet, good for working or reading for a long stretch. There's a range of beans to pick from and colorful Italian sodas for the non-coffee crowd. Easy street parking out front.

items.name: Sober Coffee House
items.blurb: A cafe in an old wooden house on a street in town, with a classic, warm, quiet feel. The focus is specialty coffee, matcha and cake, ideal if you like sitting alone and sipping slowly. Parking both out front and around the back.

items.name: Local Bean x Nor.Nan
items.blurb: A cafe plus roastery on the ground floor of an old house in the center of town, quiet and warm. They use beans straight from farms in Nan and let you choose the roast level. Sometimes they run coffee workshops, so it's good if you actually want to understand Nan coffee, not just shoot photos.

items.name: Comla Bakery
items.blurb: A minimal shop in light wood tones, clean-looking. Its strength is fresh-baked croissants, scones and cakes paired with house-roasted specialty coffee. If you're into bakery and want something baked fresh in the morning, this is the one.
items.meta: In town · coffee ฿55–85 · bakery from ฿45

items.name: Workboxes Cafe
items.blurb: Out by Kad Nan, decorated Japanese-minimal in clean white tones. Favorites here are the strong coffee, Nan tea, rose oolong, tiramisu and cheesecake. The corners inside photograph clean and pretty.

items.name: LEROY CAFE NAN
items.blurb: A shop down a small lane, decorated '90s vintage with arty details all over. The vibe is easygoing, with coffee, Indonesian tea and baked goods including fresh croissants. Good for people who like a place with its own distinct character.
items.meta: Down a lane in town · coffee around ฿55–85

items.name: Hatake Cafe
items.blurb: A Japanese-minimal cafe over near Bo Kluea, small and in town, with some green space. Besides coffee there are savory dishes to fill you up and several kinds of cake, so it's good if you want a light meal and coffee in one place. Easy parking.
items.meta: In town · coffee around ฿55–85 · food available

items.name: NAN HARMONY
items.blurb: A warm Japanese-minimal shop near Nan Hospital. Standouts are caramel butter toast, roti, matcha and coffee. Good for settling in through the afternoon, with parking at the nearby Wat Tha Chang grounds.

items.name: Luem Luen in Nan
items.blurb: A cafe plus restaurant in a classic European tone mixed with a garden, shady and relaxed. There's coffee, baked goods and proper food like khao soi, crispy pork noodles and homemade pizza, so it suits a group that wants a real meal then coffee in one spot.
items.meta: In town · coffee around ฿55–90 · main dishes available

blocks.title: Tips for a Cafe Walk Through the Old Town
blocks.html: Most shops in Nan open late-ish, around 8–9am, and close early in the evening (many shut at 5–6pm). If you want to hit several, start around the Wat Phumin area in the morning and work outward, so you get nice light and the shops aren't packed yet.

blocks.text: How to Pick the Right Cafe for You

items: Want genuine doi Nan arabica — Erabica, Local Bean x Nor.Nan and shops that clearly state they use province-grown beans, with a choice of roast level.
Working or reading for a long stretch — inlamai and Sober Coffee House are quiet and airy, good for staying a while.
Into fresh-baked goods — Comla Bakery and LEROY focus on croissants and freshly made bakes.
Coming as a group and want a real meal — Luem Luen in Nan and Hatake have main dishes too.

blocks.text: Where to Shoot Good Photos Around the Cafes

items.name: Wat Phumin
items.blurb: The starting point of the cafe district. The gateway arch and the famous Pu Man Ya Man mural are right here, and the coffee shops are a short walk out.

items.name: Pha Kong Road
items.blurb: The cafe street in the center of town, lined with wooden-house and minimal shops, with plenty to photograph as you walk.

items.name: Old City Wall & Khuang Mueang
items.blurb: In the morning the light is soft and you can get nice shots with the old wall and big trees. Close to several shops.

faq.q: Are the cafes in Nan's Old Town walkable from one another?
faq.a: Most sit within a few hundred meters to about 1 km of Wat Phumin, so you can hit several in one morning on foot. For the ones a bit farther out, like over by Kad Nan or near the hospital, driving or cycling is easier.

faq.q: Where does the coffee in Nan come from?
faq.a: Many shops in town use arabica from the doi around Nan province itself. Some roast in-house and let you choose the roast level. Ask the barista which doi the beans came from — most are happy to tell you the story.

faq.q: What time do the coffee shops in Nan open?
faq.a: Most open late-ish, around 8–9am, and close fairly early in the evening, with many shutting around 5–6pm. If you want to do several, start early in the morning and check each shop's day off before you go.

faq.q: Roughly how much is coffee at a Nan cafe?
faq.a: A cup mostly runs around ฿50–90 depending on the drink and the shop. Signature drinks or special pour-overs can be a little higher, and fresh-baked goods start around ฿45. These are rough figures from reviews and can change.

faq.q: If I don't drink coffee, are there other options?
faq.a: Almost every shop has them — matcha, Nan tea, rose oolong, Italian sodas and bakery. Some, like Hatake and Luem Luen in Nan, also have main dishes if you want a proper meal.
